svg.text: MECHANICAL LOCK (§4.3 shank — ratchet barbs; NO groove on this end)
Anchor retention (BLOCKER-3, HW.26) · mechanical_lock_zone3 · 01_01 §4.3
FRONT
Ø9
Ø1.35 bus channel
3× barb · shallow α ramp faces the LEFT end (enters PEEK first)
NO DIN-471 groove on this end — the ring as a backup was removed (§4.3 B)
SIDE
Ø9
NOTES:
1. NO DIN-471 groove on this end — the ring as a backup was removed (§4.3 B); barb base≈0.59 mm (derived h·(cotα+cotβ), §4.3 A)
2. Material: Ti-6Al-4V Grade 5. ATTENTION: 4V here is the standing baseline, not a settled choice - the V-free perimeter rule (ratified
2026-09-17, 01_02 2.5) covers this Zone-3 part, so V-free replaces 4V here if the alloy bake-off winner has an endurance limit at least
that of 4V; otherwise this part stays 4V. The material SPECIFICATION follows the process route below and is therefore not fixed here:
printed -> ASTM F2924 (AM powder bed fusion); machined from wrought bar -> a wrought Grade-5 spec, to be NAMED when the route is fixed
rather than guessed now (00_06 0 Validation Gate)
3. Process: CNC from wrought bar, OR SLM/DMLS followed by a MANDATORY HIP (01_02 1.7, Zone 3 row, ratified 2026-09-18 - this shank is the
same part as the cathode flange); build tip-down, leading-ramp-down (01_01 §4.3 A — holds for this SEPARATE print) if SLM, with supports
only under the disc; the disc's underside (the shoulder, the axial datum) is faced on the channel's setup after they come off - see
cathode_flange (ratified 2026-09-18, 00_07 HW.26)
4. Surface: ETCHED if the part is printed, as-machined if it is turned from bar - and that follows from the production ORDER, not from a
finish spec. The order INVERTED on 2026-09-17: canon forbids the bake after the PEEK press-fit (measured - at 250 C the O11 bore grows
180-217 um more than the shaft), and the bake must follow the etch it degasses, so BOTH surviving branches of 01_02 1.3 etch the BARE
part and assemble afterwards. This surface is therefore no longer inside the joint when the anchor is etched. The catalytic-face finish
of the flange (01_02 1.2, EAAE dual-scale) belongs to cem/cathode_flange.json and does NOT extend to this shank. (The consequence is
ours; the ORDER is canon.) ATTENTION - what ACCEPTANCE applies here is OPEN, and do not read the flange band onto it: the EAAE dual-scale
row of 01_02 1.2 is written for a catalytic face, whose duty is surface area, while this is a mating face of an interference fit. The
question the inversion OPENED, and which nothing has measured, is the mirror of the old one: whether an etched surface survives the
press-fit, and what the etch takes off the interference (00_07 HW.34/HW.26). Until that is answered this note states the STATE of the
surface, never a requirement for it.
5. Post-process: NO DIN-471 groove on this end: the ring as a backup was removed on both ends and this groove from the geometry (ratified
2026-09-18, 00_07 HW.26) - in the assembled stack it sat about 2.0 mm inside the PEEK sleeve and could not take a ring once pressed
6. Coating: NOT SPECIFIED, and deliberately so: the 01_02 3.6 map covers the flange catalytic face, the outer jacket and the pogo pad - this
press-fit shank is on none of those rows. Apply nothing without a verdict; the constraint here is FIT, not DET (any coating of thickness
t adds 2t of DIAMETRAL interference to a band specified in micrometres - 01_01 4.2 gives the nominal CLASS (H7/s6); the tree's band is
5-34 um diametral from tools/in_silico/lib/constants.py, and it is NOT that class but the H7/r6 read (s6 on O11 gives 10-39 um; no table
class is meant: the band is to be solved from the Lame window, ratified 2026-09-18, 00_07 HW.3). ATTENTION on its PROVENANCE, corrected
2026-09-11 (00_07 HW.3): that is a plain ISO 286 table read (H7 0/+18 + r6 +23/+34 on O11), NOT a Lame result - Lame CONSUMES the band to
get a contact pressure. 01_01 4.2 requires the drawing's micrometres to come from the Lame interference window and REJECTS a blind ISO
286 lookup, so calling the band Lame-computed dresses the rejected source in the required source's name. Re-deriving it is ratified
2026-09-18 (00_07 HW.3) - floor: the fit still holds at +40 C, ceiling: PEEK von Mises at -30 C - and waits on its inputs only; at its
MIN the 5-34 band lies BELOW that floor, so the number WILL move). Contact plating (02_02 1.2) concerns the flange pogo face only, NOT
this part - and its process is itself an open decision (02_02 1.3)
7. Lattice: Not applicable - solid shank with a central bus channel, no lattice
8. Inspect: Barb tooth geometry MEASURED against 01_01 4.3 (alpha/beta + h specified, base DERIVED, acceptance 0.40-0.60 mm); shallow alpha
ramp toward the shank tip (the end that enters the PEEK first), steep beta face toward the flange - the two ends look opposite only in
the assembled view. No groove to inspect on this end (removed 2026-09-18, 00_07 HW.26). Bus channel diameter must accept the structural
liner (01_01 1.4). ATTENTION: shank diameter is an HW.8 PLACEHOLDER, not canon - do not treat it as a frozen acceptance dimension.
Pull-out retention and the PEEK 150 C click-fit are FEA + bench (00_07 HW.3.IS), NOT drawing acceptance lines
9. Self-contained demo of the Zone-3 lock (Ø9 = HW.8 placeholder; shallow ramp toward the shank tip, §4.3 A). The cathode flange part
already carries this shank: cem/cathode_flange.json holds its own copy of these shank fields, and the same generator builds the flange's
shank from them
10. Barb pull-out (3–5× vs friction) and PEEK 150°C click-fit retention are FEA + bench (HW.3.IS), NOT asserted by this generator
